questions.question: In which year did Babur defeat the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodi, at Panipat and capture Delhi and Agra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****__1526__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

__
 
• In 1526, **Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat **and captured **Delhi and Agra**.
 
• This is called The first battle of Panipat.
 
• Babur, a Central Asian ruler and a descendant of the **Mongol conqueror Genghis Khan **invaded India and defeated the **Lodi Empire of Northern India.**
 
• Babur was invited by **Daulat Khan** Lodi to defeat** Ibrahim Lodi.**
 
• The** battle of Panipat **was between the armies of** Babur and Ibrahim Lodi.**
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi was defeated** in the battle and he **died in battle** along with 15,000 soldiers.
 
• **Babur won the war** and his troops occupied both** Delhi and Agra**, and the **Mughal empire** was started.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 The first battle of Tarain
 It was fought in 1191 between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan
 
 

 The first battle of Panipat 
 It was fought between the forces of Babur and Ibrahim Lodhi. The Battle was fought on April 21, 1526.
 
 

 The second battle of Panipat
 It was fought between Hindu Emperor Hemu Chandra Vikramaditya and Akbar. It was fought on 5th November 1556

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties was founded by Qutb ud-din Aibak?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Slave dynasty existed in India between AD 1206-1290.
 
• Slave Dynasty was established in Northern India by **Qutb-ud-Din Aibak**__, a Turkish Mamluk slave general from Central Asia.
 
• In 1206, Muhammad of Ghor, Sultan of the Ghurid Empire, was assassinated.
 
• Qutb-ud-Din Aibak became the sultan of Delhi, and that was the beginning of the Slave dynasty.
 
• Aibak rose to power when the Ghurid superior was assassinated.
 
• He became the ruler of an independent kingdom that evolved into the Delhi Sultanate ruled by the Mamluk dynasty.

questions.question: In which year was the Delhi Sultanate established?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**1206**__".

__
 
• The period between 1206 A.D. and 1526 A.D. in India's history is known as the Delhi Sultanate period. 
 
• During this period of over three hundred years, five dynasties ruled in Delhi. 
 
• These were five dynasties as follows:
 
 
• The Slave dynasty (1206-90).
 
• Khilji dynasty (1290-1320).
 
• Tughlaq dynasty (1320-1413).
 
• Sayyid dynasty (1414-51).
 
• Lodhi Dynasty (1451-1526).

• The Slave Dynasty ruled the Sub-continent for about 84 years.
 
 
• It was the first** Muslim dynasty that ruled India. Qutub-ud-din Aibak, a slave of Muhammad Ghori, who became the ruler after the death of his master, founded the Slave Dynasty.**

 
 
• He was a great builder who built the majestic** 238 feet high stone tower known as Qutub Minar in Delhi. **
 
 
 
• Razia Begum, the capable daughter of Iltutmush, was the first and the only Muslim lady who ever adorned the throne of Delhi. 
 
 
 
• **Jalal-ud-din Khilji was the founder Khilji dynasty.**
 
 
• Ala-ud-din Khilji was the first Muslim ruler whose empire covered almost the whole of India up to its extreme south.
 
 
 
• **Ghyasuddin Tughlaq, who was the Governor of Punjab **during the reign of Ala-ud-din Khilji, ascended the throne in 1320 A.D. **and founded the Tughlaq dynasty.**

questions.question: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni, raided which famous Indian temple?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Somnath Temple, Gujarat.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025 AD attacked and looted the Somnath Mandir located in Prabhas Patan near Veraval in Saurashtra** on the western coast of Gujarat.
 
• Mahmud of Ghazni was the** ruler of Afghanistan**.
 
• The plundered Somnath Mandir was rebuilt by the** Paramara king Bhoja **of Malwa and the **Solanki king Bhimdev I **of Anhilwara between 1026 and 1042 AD.

 Temple
 Location
 Brief Description
 
 
 
 

 Somnath Temple
 Gujarat, India
 One of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva, Somnath Temple is a highly revered pilgrimage site for Hindus. This historical temple is said to have been destroyed and rebuilt several times, with the present temple constructed in the Chalukya style of architecture and completed in 1951.
 
 

 Jagannath Puri Temple
 Odisha, India
 This temple is a famous and sacred Hindu pilgrimage site dedicated to Lord Jagannath, a form of Lord Vishnu. The temple is known for its annual Rath Yatra, or chariot festival, in which the three main temple deities are hauled on huge and elaborately decorated temple cars. The current temple structure was built in the 12th century.
 
 

 Yamunotri Temple
 Uttarakhand, India
 Yamunotri Temple is the first stop in the Char Dham Yatra (pilgrimage) of Uttarakhand, dedicated to Goddess Yamuna. It's situated in the Western region of Garhwal Himalayas at an altitude of 3293 meters. The shrine is surrounded by undulating peaks and thermal springs, offering stunning scenic beauty.
 
 

 Lingaraj Temple
 Odisha, India
 This ancient temple, dedicated to Harihara, a form of Shiva and Vishnu, is one of the oldest temples in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The temple dates back to the 11th century and is a masterpiece of the Orissan style of architecture. The 54.8-meter high central tower dominates the landscape.

questions.question: Which of the following musicians of medieval India is referred to as ‘Tuti - e - Hind’ and is also regarded as the father of qawwali?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amir Khusrau**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amir Khusrau** is often referred to as 'Tuti-e-Hind', which means 'The Parrot of India'.
 
• He is also regarded as the **father of qawwali**, a devotional music form associated with Sufism.
 
• Amir Khusrau was a renowned poet, musician, and scholar in medieval India and served in the courts of various rulers of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• His contributions to Indian classical music, including the introduction of new ragas and musical instruments, are highly significant.
 
• He is also credited with the invention of the tabla and the sitar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amir Khusrau** was born in 1253 AD in Patiyali, in present-day Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• He was a prolific writer and composed poetry in Persian, Hindavi, and other languages.
 
• His literary works include ghazals, masnavis, and riddles, which are still celebrated in South Asian literature.
 
• Khusrau's influence on Indian music and culture extends beyond his lifetime, with his legacy continuing to inspire musicians and poets.
 
• He played a crucial role in the cultural amalgamation of Persian and Indian traditions during his era.

questions.question: Who built the Hawa Mahal situated in Jaipur?
questions.solution:

The correct answer is __**1192.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Prithviraja III** was the last Hindu king of the **Chauhan dynasty of Delhi.**
 
• The battle between Sultan Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraja III was known as the **Second Battle of Tarain.**
 
• The defeat of Prithviraja III marked the beginning of **Muslim rule in Northern India.**
 
• Sultan Muhammad Ghori was a **Persian ruler **who founded the **Ghurid dynasty** in **Afghanistan and North India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The year 1191 is significant in Indian history as it marks the **First Battle of Tarain** in which **Prithviraja III defeated Sultan Muhammad Ghori.**
 
• The **kingdom of Sapadalaksha** was ruled by Prithviraja III who had his capital at** Ajmer** in modern-day Rajasthan. 
 
• From **1173 to 1206,** Muhammad Ghori, a member of the Ghurid dynasty based in what is now central **Afghanistan,** was in charge.
 
• Up until Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad's passing in** 1203**, Muhammad of Ghor and his older brother Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad held dynastic rule.

• State Legislature
 
• High Courts
 
• Secretariat buildings of the States or the Union territories

questions.question: Who among the following was defeated in the Battle of Kannauj in 1540?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Kannauj** was fought between the **Mughal Emperor Humayun** and the **Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri** in **1540.**
 
• Sher Shah Suri emerged **victorious in the battle** and** Humayun** was forced to** flee to Iran**.
 
• The battle is considered as a turning point in the history of India as it marked the** end of the Mughal rule **and the beginning of the **Sur dynasty.**
 
• Sher Shah Suri went on to establish a** strong administration** and introduced various reforms, such as the introduction of the **rupee as a currency** and the construction of the **Grand Trunk Road.**
 
• **Akbar,** who was the son of **Humayun,** later **defeated the Sur dynasty **and established the **Mughal rule **in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hemu,** also known as Hemchandra Vikramaditya, was a** Hindu king** who ruled over **Delhi **in the **16th century.**
 
• **Sher Shah Suri** was a **Pashtun warrior **who rose to power after defeating the **Mughal Emperor Humayun.**
 
 
• He is known for his **administrative and military reforms **and is considered as one of the greatest rulers of **medieval India. **
 
 
 
• **Akbar** was the **third Mughal Emperor **who ruled over India from **1556 to 1605.**
 
 
• He is known for his** religious tolerance, military conquests, and cultural achievements.**
 
 
 
• **Humayun **was the **second Mughal Emperor** who ruled over India from **1530 to 1540 **and from** 1555 to 1556.**
 
 
• He was known for his** military failures** and was forced to flee to Iran after his defeat in the Battle of Kannauj.
